races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Austrian Theory
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up performer for Tim Easterby, ridden by the trainer's son Mr Thomas Easterby (3lb claim); has zero wins and just one place from 10 runs on similar going, making his form in this context poor, and his best trip appears shorter than 1m4f given his recent history over 9-12f.

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: Has won twice and placed four times from seven runs on Good ground and arrives as the race's lone front runner, which is a significant tactical asset; racing labelled as out of role given its natural front-running tendency mapped as prominent, but in practice it will simply lead unchallenged — the discount on its chance relates to whether it can sustain the effort over 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Mariner
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good ground for Jennie Candlish most recently and has a strong overall W/P record (3 wins, 5 places from 10 good-ground runs); a natural hold-up type who wears a tongue-strap and headgear combination, and the compressed pace scenario may limit his finishing kick if the race does not develop into a genuine test.

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old Jim Goldie-trained veteran whose recent form reads 00665, with no win or place from his last five in Good-ground company; despite being a natural hold-up horse, he is pressed into a midfield role here because the rear of the field is congested — his recent trajectory and age make it hard to be optimistic regardless of race shape.

runners_data.name: Stellarmasterpiece
runners_data.note: Has won five times at distances between 14f and 18f on Good ground — outstanding stamina credentials — and her headgear (p) suggests she is sharp and switched on; Micky Hammond's T14 record of 0/3 is quiet, but Stellarmasterpiece's own course-and-distance profile at marathon trips in this going is the standout data point in the field.

runners_data.name: Shahbaz
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's 6-year-old has run six times at 12f on Good or Standard ground with only one win and one place to show; a genuine hold-up type in the data, mapped to midfield because the field is back-heavy, which means he is unlikely to see out the race in the way his style demands — T14 of 0/21 adds little confidence.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 6-year-old has three wins and seven places from 11 runs on Good ground and finished first or second in four of her last five starts over 10f; a prominent-style runner with a 5lb-claiming amateur aboard, and her consistency on this going and at this general trip makes her one of the more reliable pieces of form in the race, though stepping up to 1m4f is a query.

races.paceDynamic: Super Hit is the one confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead in a seven-runner field, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Catterick. Stellarmasterpiece and Star Start are both prominent types who will track closely, creating a small lead group that sets a steady rather than searching tempo, which typically compresses the field and makes it hard for true hold-up horses to generate enough momentum late. This field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Spanish Hustle and Shahbaz are natural closers but both are mapped to midfield because there is simply no room for all of them to settle as deep as they would ideally prefer, which undermines their late-run threat. With the pace controlled and measured, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can press Super Hit from a handy position and pounce in the final two furlongs without needing a strong pace injection to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit dictates an uncontested, even tempo and the prominent holders track without disrupting the rhythm.
scenarios.body: Super Hit sets a comfortable pace through the long Catterick straight, and the prominent brigade — Stellarmasterpiece and Star Start — sit close enough to challenge entering the final quarter-mile without burning energy in a chase. Horses with strong Good-ground form at this type of trip who race handily are squarely in their element here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent horses makes a forward move turning for home and catches Super Hit flat-footed.
scenarios.body: Stellarmasterpiece, a five-time winner who has placed consistently at longer trips in similar going, has the stamina reserves to press hard from 2f out and outbattle Super Hit if the leader loses momentum. Star Start's consistent Good-ground form over similar trips means she can also sustain a run from a handy position if the front-runner weakens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo quickens mid-race and creates enough of a true test to bring a closer into play in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mariner is the hold-up runner most likely to benefit, having the most recent win record over Good ground at 10f and sitting naturally just off the pace in what is a compressed field — his trainer Jennie Candlish has a strong T14 strike rate. Austrian Theory has similar hold-up credentials but a poorer recent record in comparable conditions (0 wins from 10 runs on similar going), limiting his claims.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly strong gallop develops and Spanish Hustle or Shahbaz find themselves closer than expected with energy to burn.
scenarios.body: Spanish Hustle and Shahbaz are natural hold-up horses forced to race nearer the pace than suits them, and their recent form strings (including multiple out-of-the-money finishes) suggest they are vulnerable at current level on Good ground. A truly end-to-end gallop is the only way their stamina could be weaponised, but that depends on conditions that seem unlikely given the lone front-runner setup.

watchPoints.text: Super Hit's ability to control the pace entirely unchallenged is the race's hinge — if he bowls along at an uncontested canter, watch whether Stellarmasterpiece or Star Start have the courage to go with him early enough to prevent a soft lead turning into an unassailable one.

Stellarmasterpiece holds her best form over distances notably longer than 1m4f (her five wins are all at 16f-18f) — watch whether she has enough speed to compete at this shorter trip if the pace is truly sedate, or whether she stays on best when others have emptied.

Spanish Hustle and Shahbaz are both natural hold-up horses forced to race closer than ideal; if either drifts back to their true position at the rear, they may be too far off the pace in a seven-runner field running at a sustainable tempo to mount any meaningful challenge.

Star Start's amateur jockey Miss Charli Parker carries a 5lb claim, which has a meaningful weight impact at this level — watch whether the claim translates into a positional advantage given Star Start's naturally prominent style and consistent Good-ground record.

Mariner's trainer Jennie Candlish has posted a 4/12 T14 strike rate (33%), which is strong context — watch whether Mariner is produced fresh and forward, as a hold-up horse who needs a true pace to pounce may be frustrated by the likely tempo.

races.name: Well-Earned Retirement Neal Kidd Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Harry's Pop
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with consistent placed efforts at 6f on good ground; Sam James a strong booking for Dylan Cunha who has been in form (T14: 3/23); 14 days since last run is a short, fit turnaround, and tracking the likely leader is a natural tactical fit here.

runners_data.name: Aura Of Melania
runners_data.note: Has placed on good ground at 6f and 7f, showing she handles the surface; true hold-up style that ideally needs cover and a strong pace to close into, which this race may not fully provide; 21 days since last run for Roger Fell is routine.

runners_data.name: Eevee Star
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell yard in fine form (T14: 8/21) and Oisin Orr is a reliable northern partner; placed twice at 6f on good ground gives solid going credentials, but her genuine hold-up style means she needs the race to set up for a late run that a slow pace here may not deliver.

runners_data.name: Cheeky Chesca
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and sole pace-setter in this field; headgear worn, Tim Easterby handler — a combination that often signals a sharper early effort; recent form figures (9,7,7) are poor but those were likely pace-affected races whereas here she controls the fractions entirely.

runners_data.name: Soldier's Echo
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer runner with only three runs, modest form (7,9,6), and a 28-day break; genuinely prefers to come from behind but the overcrowded hold-up section means he is likely to race closer than ideal — the style mismatch tempers any expectations from this position.

runners_data.name: Invicta Rose
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster yard (T14: 2/19) with Garritty up; five consecutive races without placing and form figures showing little improvement at 6f on good ground; naturally wants to settle and come late, which is a tough ask when the shape here does not generate a strong pace for hold-up horses to key off.

runners_data.name: So Tempting
runners_data.note: Tom Ward sends her here with headgear flag noted, which may indicate a forward-going tweak to her usual hold-up profile; ran second at 6f on good early in her career and that form holds appeal, but subsequent runs have deteriorated and the field congestion at the rear limits her natural scope.

runners_data.name: Athos
runners_data.note: John Butler yard solid (T14: 7/24) and Joanna Mason a capable northern claimer; form has been entirely on standard/good ground at 6f-7f with modest placings; races from the back in the truest sense and with three hold-up rivals ahead of her on the map she faces a crowded late lane with limited likelihood of a clear run.

races.paceDynamic: Cheeky Chesca is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner 2yo nursery and, with no obvious rival to challenge for the early lead, David Allan can dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the front at Catterick's 6f. Good ground suits the pace-setter and, with no pressing from behind, fractions are unlikely to be excessive, meaning the lead will not be surrendered cheaply. Harry's Pop is the only prominent-style runner to her outside, capable of tracking but not likely to fire the pace into a genuine test. This shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles — those who can sit close to the action without burning energy, as the steady early tempo will not set up a deep late surge for true closers. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Soldier's Echo, Invicta Rose, So Tempting, and Athos are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and of these Soldier's Echo (Hugo Palmer, PJ McDonald-level syndicate backing) and So Tempting (headgear, prior form figure) are most likely to press forward and secure a workable position, though none can realistically lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chesca Leads, Front Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Cheeky Chesca secures an uncontested lead and sets a controlled, honest gallop that suits the prominent profile.
scenarios.body: David Allan settles Cheeky Chesca in front without pressure and the pace is measured enough to hold rivals at bay into the Catterick straight; the horse's recent placed form in similar conditions underpins this. Harry's Pop, tracking throughout, is ideally positioned to challenge and benefit if the leader ties up, while the hold-up horses are left with too little ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Cheeky Chesca's gallop is sustainable but not winning-fast and Harry's Pop or a horse pressing the pace picks up sharply in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Harry's Pop, with recent 6f good-ground form and Sam James riding, sits a length off the leader and finds a decisive gear when asked at the two-furlong pole; the uncomplicated pace shape means no energy is wasted and the prominent runners have full fuel reserves for the finish. Aura Of Melania, who has placed on good ground at this trip, could also deliver a strong late challenge from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and bunches the field, creating a compressed finish where a hold-up runner can weave through.
scenarios.body: A slow tempo collapses the gaps and Eevee Star or Aura Of Melania, both rated on good ground at this trip with placed form, can find a line through tired rivals in the final furlong; this scenario is limited in likelihood because the hold-up runners are largely redistributed types not truly racing from their natural position. So Tempting, who has a prior second at 6f on good, is the most credible hold-up beneficiary if ground is covered.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Fades, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Cheeky Chesca's recent poor form (three consecutive finishes of 7th, 9th, 7th) resurfaces and the pace collapses late, creating a wide-open finish.
scenarios.body: With the leader weakening inside the final furlong, the field closes in a bunch and any prominent or midfield horse with residual energy can grab the spoils; Harry's Pop and Eevee Star, both capable of holding a good position, would be best placed to scoop a messy finish. The redistribution of so many hold-up types means this scenario is unlikely to deliver a clean late flourish from the back.

watchPoints.text: Watch Cheeky Chesca's early strides — if she breaks cleanly and David Allan sends her straight to the front without a chase, the race is effectively over as a tactical contest and all positional bets are set within the first furlong.

Monitor Harry's Pop's position at the break; if Sam James allows him to drift back beyond second or third, a prominent-style horse loses his key advantage and the race shape becomes far more open for the hold-up runners.

So Tempting carries headgear for the first time or as a flag — watch the paddock for any significant change in demeanour, as a more forward-going run from her would compress the midfield and potentially unsettle Cheeky Chesca's rhythm.

With four hold-up types redistributed to midfield, watch for early crowding on the inside rail as Catterick's 6f chute narrows; a bumped or checked midfield runner could lose significant ground before the race develops its natural shape.

Eevee Star's trainer Edward Bethell is running at a strong 8/21 strike rate over 14 days — note if the market moves for her pre-race, as yard form is a live angle even if the race shape is not ideal for her natural style.

races.name: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a recent win at 5f on Good (11 days ago), but all last five runs have been at 5f — the step up to 6f here is an untested extra furlong that may blunt the finishing kick P J McDonald will be looking to deploy late.

runners_data.name: Daytona Lady
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old has solid recent form over this 6f trip but her sim-going record on Good (0W1P in 2 runs) is thin compared to her Stansted work; James Sullivan will need a genuine pace to chase from hold-up, which this race should provide, though Catterick form is absent from her last five.

runners_data.name: Good Karma
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in fine recent form — a 7f win and a 7f placed run immediately before this — and Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim could be significant at these weights; the drop back to 6f from 7f winning form suggests a horse in good shape with plenty of stamina in reserve.

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: The standout front-runner on Good ground with 3 wins and 8 places from 11 similar-going starts; Tracy Waggott has a 1/2 T14 strike rate suggesting a live runner, and her recent Catterick win at 6f on Good is directly transferable — the key question is whether Quercus's presence forces her to burn too much early.

runners_data.name: Quercus
runners_data.note: Ann Duffield's nine-year-old has not won in recent outings (5th, 6th, 5th, 12th) despite a good sim-going record (1W3P), and 33 days since last run adds a fitness query; Shane Gray takes over and he will need Quercus to lead cleanly without being pressured by Miss Rainbow if he is to have any realistic chance.

runners_data.name: One Of Our Own
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies's six-year-old has a solid Catterick profile with multiple Good-ground placed runs and a win at 6f in this class; Andrew Mullen is familiar with the horse (T14: 0/6 but consistent placer), and the hold-up style suits a contested-pace race if he can find a clear run in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old boasts an impressive sim-going record (3W4P in 13 Good runs) and won over this course and distance recently; although his true instinct is to come from off the pace, the crowded hold-up section means David Allan will likely have to push him closer to midfield, slightly compromising the role he performs best.

runners_data.name: Edmond Halley
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old is lightly frighted at hold-up tactics but his recent form (3/6f Soft, then 5th, 7th, 11th, 10th) shows a drop in consistency; the short 7-day turnaround is worth noting, and Oisin Orr will find him racing further forward than ideal given the congestion at the rear — his best chance depends on a longer-distance stamina test he may not get here at 6f.

runners_data.name: Papa Don't Preach
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's seven-year-old is a consistent prominent runner over 5f, and all five recent runs have been at 5f on Good — the step up to 6f is unproven and may just blunt the finishing speed William Pyle will want to use from a prominent position; solid recent placed form (0W4P) but no win since OR was higher.

races.paceDynamic: Quercus and Miss Rainbow are both confirmed front-runners over this 6f Catterick trip on Good ground, meaning the early gallop will be genuinely contested from the gates — neither is the type to yield and settle behind the other. That tussle for the lead creates an honest, pressured pace that is unlikely to collapse into a dawdle, setting up a race where stamina and resolution in the final furlong become decisive. The field also contains more hold-up horses than can all settle naturally at the rear — Edmond Halley and Barmyblade are genuine late types redistributed to midfield on the map because Miss Rainbow and Quercus absorb the front positions, meaning those two will not be racing from their truest vantage point. This shape — two front-runners burning fuel early on a flat course — classically favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can track a strong pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs rather than closers who need a truly searching gallop they can target from well off it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Quercus and Miss Rainbow push each other hard from the off, the honest gallop hands an advantage to the prominent trackers who save a length or two early.
scenarios.body: The pace duel burns both leaders out approaching the final furlong, leaving the prominent chasers — particularly Good Karma and Papa Don't Preach — in the ideal position to swoop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Survives Contested Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner (Miss Rainbow most likely given her Good-ground record of 3W8P) establishes a marginal break and controls the tempo rather than being fully pressured.
scenarios.body: Miss Rainbow's strong sim-going form (11 runs on Good, 3 wins) and recent Catterick win give her the profile to dictate from the front and hold on; a cleaner break from Quercus — who has faded from the lead recently — would allow her to conserve enough to last home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly searching and creates a clear gap between the spent leaders and the pack, allowing a horse tracking from mid-division to deliver a telling run through.
scenarios.body: One Of Our Own has solid Catterick form (1W3P on Good) and Andrew Mullen knows the track; Good Karma's recent win at 7f suggests they will stay and finish strongly if the pace softens the leaders sufficiently.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners utterly collapse and the closing kick of genuine hold-up types is rewarded — but this shape is markedly less likely given Barmyblade and Edmond Halley are racing out of their natural deep position.
scenarios.body: Barmyblade has the form (3W4P on Good in 13 runs) to be dangerous if everything sets up perfectly, but being pushed forward from their true hold-up role compromises both him and Edmond Halley's ability to deliver the late surge they need.

watchPoints.text: Quercus and Miss Rainbow — watch the first furlong closely; if both are fully committed to the lead from the gates, the pace could be falsely fast and set the race up for the prominent-to-midfield chasers at the expense of both front-runners.

Barmyblade and Edmond Halley — both are true hold-up types who will be pushed closer to midfield than they prefer; if either finds a pocket or gets shuffled back completely, their chance changes shape dramatically and the closing finish scenario becomes either more or less credible depending on what gap materialises.

Good Karma — trainer John David Riches has only had 2 runners in 14 days and 0 winners; watch the market for any drift that might signal the step down from 7f to 6f has been misjudged, even though the form reads well.

Daytona Lady — James Sullivan will need a strong pace to deliver a meaningful hold-up finish; if either front-runner goes easy early, Daytona Lady's chance diminishes significantly as her sim-going numbers on Good are thin.

Papa Don't Preach — all recent form is over 5f, and this 6f trip on Good ground at Catterick is untested territory; watch how William Pyle positions him early — if he is further back than his P-style suggests, the extra furlong could simply find him out.

races.name: Constant Security Services Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Star Noir
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f performer who has placed on Good ground before, making her the most likely horse to race prominently behind Preferred; trainer T14 strike rate (2/27) is modest and she has not run since 76 days ago, but her sim-going form (2 place finishes from 7) is encouraging for this surface.

runners_data.name: Top Lad
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse from the same Easterby yard with a poor record — 0 wins, 0 places on similar going from 7 runs — who typically drops to the rear and relies on others to burn; last ran 38 days ago but has no form at this 5f trip and is poorly placed tactically given the expected moderate tempo.

runners_data.name: Rocktoun Heart
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 4-year-old with no accessible form data and style entirely unknown, carrying a notional OR=120; trainer Linda Perratt has a reasonable T14 record (2/11) and Paul Mulrennan is an experienced northern jockey, but this is a significant unknown quantity and fitness must be taken on trust.

runners_data.name: Miss Tino
runners_data.note: Debutant with no published form, unknown running style, and a notional OR=120; the Thompson yard has no T14 runners returned, making stable fitness harder to gauge, and Barry McHugh will need to have been given clear instructions about how to deploy her given the complete absence of race evidence.

runners_data.name: Night Shining
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who has placed once on Good ground and posted four consecutive fourth-place finishes, suggesting a reliable but uninspired profile; wears headgear (tongue-tie) and is freshened from a 14-day break under Pat Cosgrave, though the moderate expected pace over 5f at Catterick makes a late run from off the bridle difficult to land.

runners_data.name: Preferred
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field and a big player in this race shape; trained by James Tate and ridden by P J McDonald, he returns from a 206-day absence which is the one notable risk, but three runners in two starts suggest a horse who has been campaigned lightly and may be fit to go; has run 6f on Standard so dropping to 5f turf on Good is an open question.

races.paceDynamic: Preferred is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no other genuine pace-setter in the six-runner field, P J McDonald can dictate terms from the off at a tempo entirely of his own choosing over this 5f Catterick straight. Star Noir (prominent) is the only other runner likely to race close to the pace, but she is not a natural leader and will not pressure Preferred into a frantic gallop — meaning the pace is almost certain to be controlled and sustainable rather than suicidal. Night Shining and Top Lad are both hold-up types who will need the front two to tie each other up, a scenario that simply is not on the cards here. Rocktoun Heart and Miss Tino are unknown quantities on style, but even if one tracks up prominently, Preferred already holds the rail advantage and the initiative. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner and prominent racer: a measured pace with no sustained challenge allows Preferred to conserve energy and quicken off the bend, and any horse that can slot in just behind the leader and travel within the tempo is next best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Preferred Controls and Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Preferred settles into a comfortable rhythm up front and faces no sustained early pressure from any rival.
scenarios.body: McDonald sets an uncontested, measured pace and hits the rising ground towards the line with a full tank; horses held up off the pace have too much ground to make up in the time available over 5f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Outstays Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Star Noir tracks Preferred relentlessly and outruns the leader in the final furlong under Billy Garritty.
scenarios.body: Star Noir has placed twice on Good ground at 5f and can race prominently enough to benefit from a true but moderate gallop; if Preferred's long absence (206 days) blunts her finishing effort, Star Noir is best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Finishes Fast Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and Night Shining produces a sustained run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Night Shining has placed on Good ground over 5f and has been running consistently in the frame; Pat Cosgrave will need the front end to empty in the final 100 yards, which is the least likely scenario given Preferred's solo lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced debutants — Rocktoun Heart or Miss Tino — possesses significantly superior raw ability and runs a big first race.
scenarios.body: With OR=120 on both, their handicap marks are notional and either could hold unexposed talent, but style and fitness unknowns make this the most speculative outcome; a forward-going display from either would be required to overcome the experience advantage held by Preferred.

watchPoints.text: Preferred's 206-day absence is the single biggest threat to the dominant scenario — watch the market move and any reports of stable form before betting on the pace-controlling scenario.

Rocktoun Heart and Miss Tino carry notional OR=120 ratings that could mask genuine ability; if either drifts forward in running unexpectedly, the race shape becomes less predictable than the single-leader read suggests.

Star Noir's trainer T14 strike rate of 2/27 (Michael & David Easterby) is low — if the horse is not at peak fitness after 76 days off, the prominent position she is expected to fill goes unfilled and the race becomes a solo procession for Preferred.

Night Shining has posted four consecutive fourth-place finishes, suggesting a horse who fills a place frame without winning — Cosgrave may adopt a more aggressive hold-up tactic if he has confidence in a strong late move, but the tempo must quicken to help him.

Top Lad has zero wins and zero places on similar going from seven attempts — note whether Joanna Mason takes an unconventionally forward position to counteract the hold-up style, which would represent a significant departure from the horse's historical profile.

races.name: racingtv.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with a sharp win at 5f on Good (1/5f/GOO in hist) and good recent course form; Adrian Nicholls yard quiet on 0/7 over 14 days, but this horse suits its own running style and a genuinely run race.

runners_data.name: Emperor's Son
runners_data.note: Hold-up type dropped back to 5f after placing work at 6f; Joanna Mason takes over 44 days after last run, and the Standish-going runs (STA) are a slight unknown, though Good form is limited to one win from five efforts.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner running just three days after its last start, which warrants monitoring for freshness; 1W2P from 6 Good-ground runs shows it can win from the front, but the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag notes it is racing slightly out of its natural role given the competitive company for the lead.

runners_data.name: Miss Brazen
runners_data.note: 62 days off the track is notable, but Michael & David Easterby send her out with a 2/27 T14 strike rate and she has compelling 5f Good form (2W5P from 14 similar-going runs); a genuine hold-up horse who needs the race to be run honestly.

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr yard in form (4/25 T14), 12 days between runs suggests she is fit and ready; naturally prominent and has placed six times at 5f on Good, making her one of the most likely horses to secure a viable prominent position.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends her out 16 days fresh with a strong T14 rate (6/79), and she is a genuine prominent type with 2W6P on similar going; wears headgear (p) and is one of the best placed horses to slot in just behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Beaumadier
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane has two winners in 14 days and this six-year-old shows consistent placing form (0W2P from 4 Good runs), but its true hold-up nature means the midfield map position understates the ground it will need to make up — Hope Regan's 7lb claim is a plus if she gets a clear run.

runners_data.name: Staniel Cay
runners_data.note: Three-year-old lightly raced (96 days off) with a win at 5f Good (1/5f/GOO hist), but fundamentally a hold-up runner who will not be positioned where the map shows; Grant Tuer's yard is quiet and the long absence adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's second runner in the race (alongside Betweenthesticks), and Tom Eaves rides a horse that has genuine Good-ground 5f ability (1W2P from 8 similar runs); despite the midfield mapping, it is a true closer needing a strong pace — OR drop to 58 gives it weight relief.

runners_data.name: Irish Dancer
runners_data.note: Prominent type wearing a tongue-strap, placed twice at 5f on Good recently (2/5f/GOO, 3/5f/GOO); Zak Wheatley takes over for Declan Carroll and this horse is the most likely to push Our Absent Friends early, which could help or hinder depending on how hard it goes.

runners_data.name: Cheerleader
runners_data.note: Tina Jackson's four-year-old has a 2/5f/GOO in her recent history but is a hold-up horse forced into a midfield slot by the congestion at the rear; Andrew Mullen rides and the 21-day break is straightforward, but the style-fit discount (0.92) reflects that she is unlikely to get her ideal run from off the pace in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Our Absent Friends is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 5f handicap at Catterick, and with no serious challenger for the lead expected to push hard from the gates, she is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground. Betweenthesticks, Canaria Queen, and Irish Dancer are the principal prominent types who will look to track closely in the first two furlongs, putting some pressure on the pace without necessarily forcing a scorching tempo. The remainder — Tees Aggregates, Emperor's Son, Miss Brazen, and several redistributed hold-up horses — will be racing from midfield or off the pace, needing the front to come back to them. This race shape, with one front-runner dictating at a manageable tempo, moderately favours prominent racers who can sit just behind the leader and pounce, rather than deep closers, as a genuinely slow pace could see Our Absent Friends steal an uncontested advantage; the field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, and Beaumadier, Staniel Cay, Invincible Crown, and Cheerleader are all true hold-up horses shuffled forward on the map — of the prominent slots, Betweenthesticks and Canaria Queen are most likely to actually secure their favoured position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Our Absent Friends sets a sustainable, uncontested pace and the prominent trackers get a clean run to challenge at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Our Absent Friends dictates a measured gallop and the horses sitting just behind — Betweenthesticks and Canaria Queen — get the ideal racing position to pounce as the field straightens; on Good ground with no pace war, energy is preserved and those in the first two lengths of the leader get first run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Steals Race
scenarios.trigger: If Our Absent Friends gets completely uncontested and the prominent types fail to apply any meaningful pressure before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no challenger prepared to go with her early, Our Absent Friends bowls along at her own pace and simply has too much in reserve when others try to close; her 5f Good-ground course form (1/5f/GOO in recent history) makes this a live possibility.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Types Run On
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely fast enough to cause the front and prominent runners to tie up in the final 100 yards, allowing closers to mop up.
scenarios.body: This would require more early pressure than the map suggests is likely, but Miss Brazen or Tees Aggregates — both with genuine hold-up profiles and strong form at 5f on Good — could be the beneficiaries if the race is run at an unusually honest tempo; their ability to finish off 5f strongly on this going gives them a narrow window.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Break, Scrambled Order
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses break sharply and contest the early lead, creating an uncharacteristically pressured pace for this field.
scenarios.body: A messy early scramble would scramble the expected race shape, burning out the front and prominent types and theoretically benefiting deeper closers, but the redistributed hold-up horses (Beaumadier, Staniel Cay, Invincible Crown, Cheerleader) are not truly positioned for this shape and their style-fit discounts make this scenario the least likely to deliver a hold-up winner.

watchPoints.text: Our Absent Friends runs just 3 days after her last outing — monitor market moves for any sign the yard is concerned about her freshness or if she shows any signs of being below par in the parade ring.

Betweenthesticks and Canaria Queen may both attempt to push forward from the gates, potentially creating a brief contested period for second position that could burn more energy than the pace map suggests — watch the early furlong for how keenly they travel.
Staniel Cay's 96-day absence is the longest in the field; Grant Tuer's yard has only 1 winner from 8 runs over 14 days and this horse's readiness after a break is a genuine unknown at this distance.

Miss Brazen's 62-day layoff combined with the Easterby 2/27 T14 strike rate means she may need this run to find peak fitness — watch whether she is strongly supported in the market as a sign the yard is confident she is ready.

Hope Regan's 7lb claim on Beaumadier is worth noting if the race develops into a strong-pace scenario — the weight advantage could be significant for a horse forced to make up ground from further back than it would ideally prefer.

races.name: Racing Again 26th August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Folkene
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Roger Fell, returning after 74 days off which is a notable absence for a horse that needs things to fall right anyway; best form at 7f on Good is there (1 win, 1 place from 7 applicable runs) but needs the prominent group to combust ahead of her with Oisin McSweeney finding clear air late.

runners_data.name: Evocative Spark
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer with strong 7f Good-ground credentials (three wins from 15 similar-going runs) and a return just 10 days ago keeping him sharp; headgear visor worn, and Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim takes weight off, but he'll have to fight hard for a clean position in an unusually congested prominent group.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: In-form 5yo on a four-race winning streak, four wins from nine similar-going runs, and trained by Iain Jardine who has fired in three winners from 28 runners in the last 14 days; headgear (hood) worn throughout the run and Shay Farmer's 5lb claim adds appeal — one of the most credible threats to the leader if he can slot cleanly into the prominent tier.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the race-shaper — recent form of 2-2-3 in similar conditions is solid, and Tristan Davidson sends him back quickly after just 9 days, suggesting he is in a good rhythm; headgear (blinkers) keeps him focused and Jack Garritty will look to coast into a simple lead with no rival willing to press.

runners_data.name: Carolus Magnus
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer who won over this exact course and distance on Good ground recently, giving him the strongest C&D profile in the field; Joanna Mason knows the track well and trainer Easterby has had two winners from 27 runners in the past 14 days — gets the run of things if Runninsonofagun sets a moderate tempo.

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has hit the frame in four of his last five on Good at 7f, running in blinkers (hg: b) to keep him honest; trained by Katie Scott with Oisin Orr aboard, he carries no claim at 136lbs but profiles as a horse who can capitalise if the congestion breaks kindly, though his lack of a recent win (0 from 8 similar runs) is a concern.

runners_data.name: No Return
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by Charlie Johnston, whose T14 strike-rate of 5/31 is the strongest in the field among closers; dropping back to 7f after a run of 6f efforts, and this distance step is interesting, but the race shape with one leader and a compressed midfield does not naturally set up a fast-final-furlong for horses coming from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Willolarupi
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Declan Carroll who has been mixing 5-7f distances, and the form string of 4-3-5-5-6 suggests consistency without the winning touch; 31 days off is manageable but Zak Wheatley faces a tough task finding a gap through a congested midfield from the rear — suited only if the race truly falls apart up front.

runners_data.name: Vince Le Prince
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a genuine hold-up racing style — his best 7f Good-ground form (2nd, 3rd among 10 similar-going runs) emerges when allowed to finish into tired horses, but in this field he has been pushed forward into a midfield mapping he wouldn't naturally occupy; Tim Easterby's prolific T14 return (6/79) keeps him on the radar, yet the style-fit tension here is real and tempering.

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old won last time out (1/7f/Good) which brings him into the race with momentum, and Carr has four winners from 25 recent runners; despite that form uptick, he is a true hold-up type bumped into midfield by congestion at the rear, meaning his winning run came in a race shape he may not be able to replicate here under the same conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Runninsonofagun is the sole confirmed front-runner and should lead from the outset at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over Catterick's 7f on Good ground, giving Jack Garritty the chance to dictate his own terms without any true rival prepared to push him early. Behind him, there is significant congestion in the prominent positions — Evocative Spark, Classy Clarets, Carolus Magnus, and Black Storm all want to race close to the pace, meaning that group of four will be scrapping for the same two or three slots from the first furlong, creating traffic danger and potential interference between the 2f and 3f markers. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the field can cleanly accommodate — Vince Le Prince and Emerald Army are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield because too many closers are chasing too few positions at the back, meaning their chance depends on a race shape that may not be run to suit them. This setup — one composed leader, a compressed prominent group scrapping behind — strongly favours horses who can track the pace cleanly in second or third without getting involved in the prominent scramble, and those riders disciplined enough to find clear daylight before the final 2f will have the material advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Runninsonofagun Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Runninsonofagun is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and the prominent group cancel each other out with their congestion.
scenarios.body: Runninsonofagun settles into a rhythm under Jack Garritty with no rival willing to burn petrol pressing him, leaving the race to be decided by who picks off the prominent bunch cleanest in the final 2f; horses that can track him at one-two lengths clear of the prominent jostle will have the decisive position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Suits Freshest
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion behind the leader unsettles the pace horses and one prominent type finds a gap at the 2f pole to sprint clear.
scenarios.body: The four prominent horses tangling for position will create a ragged passage through the middle stages, and the freshest or widest-drawn of them breaks clear as the others check each other; Classy Clarets' recent four-timer form and Evocative Spark's strong return-to-7f record both suit this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates a truly strung-out, fast-run middle section that burns off the pace-placed horses and leaves the race open for closers.
scenarios.body: Folkene or No Return would need a genuine collapse of the prominent group ahead of them and a clean run from the outside approaching the final 1f, which is possible but depends on a pace that Runninsonofagun has no reason to force; these closers have the right going credentials on the day but the race shape is not set up to deliver them a wall of tired horses to pass.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Drifters Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If traffic chaos in the prominent group and a slow final furlong collapses the field into a tight finish and a redistributed hold-up type finds an unexpected gap.
scenarios.body: Vince Le Prince and Emerald Army are true hold-up horses racing out of their natural role here, and this scenario requires an unlikely combination of pace collapse, clean passage, and a fast-finishing effort from horses not in their ideal position; the style-fit discount is significant and this scenario is low-probability precisely because neither horse is truly placed to run its race.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion between Evocative Spark, Classy Clarets, Carolus Magnus, and Black Storm is the biggest single danger point — watch the first 2f for bumping or checking as four horses chase the same two positions directly behind Runninsonofagun.

Vince Le Prince and Emerald Army are both racing out of their natural hold-up role mapped into midfield — if either gets squeezed in the bunched middle stages they have no natural early speed reserve to recover position.

Classy Clarets carries hood headgear on a four-race winning run, but at OR=69 she is already 3lbs clear of the field's average and a rise in class context means the task gets harder even with Shay Farmer's 5lb claim helping neutralise that.

Runninsonofagun returns just 9 days after his last run and also wears blinkers — if he shows any reluctance to stride on early or settles slower than his natural rhythm, the entire pace dynamic shifts and the prominent group behind him becomes the effective pace-setters.

No Return is the sole runner dropping from a run of 6f starts back to 7f — watch whether PJ McDonald attempts to exploit any early position over the trip rather than defaulting to a hold-up role, as that tactical shift would reshuffle the prominent order.
